citation: Beyond the classroom: how parents view motivation as a key to self-directed learning in township schools (Siziba, Geduld & Du Toit-Brits, Frontiers in Education, 2025)
mechanisms: Connectivity is treated as essential infrastructure because a friendly learning environment requires reliable access to information.

Parents own the motivating role — prompting, monitoring schoolwork, and authoring their own target-and-reward incentive schemes — because children are seen to rely on external regulation to initiate effort.
Fatigue and logistical constraints limit capacity because work and household duties exhaust the energy required for homework assistance.
Parental support is supplementary because determined children initiate their own study and only request help when stuck.
Motivational interventions are viewed as insufficient because structural unemployment and developmental rebellion override individual encouragement.
evaluative_rules: Judge a learning environment by its connectivity and access to information.
Set the targets and attach the rewards yourself when a child lacks initiative — motivating is the parent's own job, done through parent-authored standards and incentives.
Acknowledge that fatigue and logistics limit the capacity to assist with schoolwork.
Provide targeted assistance only when requested, respecting the child's existing agency.
Recognize that external structural barriers may outweigh individual motivational efforts.
objection_patterns: Will this require more time than I have after work and chores?
Is my child motivated enough to use this without constant shouting?
Does this account for the lack of jobs even for graduates?
Am I just topping on what they already do, or doing it for them?
confidence: Single-district qualitative interviews with 10 township parents (Sebokeng West, Gauteng); educated parents overrepresented in articulate responses; mechanisms durable, magnitudes and prevalence unknown
